messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Information:
Name: 16-Year-Old Male
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course: 
The patient was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of intellectual deficiency, proximal myopathy, and alterations in liver tests. Panel A was used for diagnostic purposes, which detected the presence of the hemizygous variant c.741+1G > A, described as pathogenic in HGMD CS003703.
During the hospital stay, the patient received appropriate medical attention. The patient was provided with standard care and treatment for the associated symptoms. The patient's overall health was closely monitored throughout the hospital stay, and there were no major health incidents.
A multidisciplinary team of doctors and medical professionals closely followed the patient's progress and offered medical care accordingly.

Discharge Instructions:
The patient is being discharged from the hospital with instructions to closely monitor his health and to follow up with his primary physician and/or cardiologist. The patient should avoid strenuous exercise, and any new or concerning symptoms should be reported to the physician immediately. The patient has been instructed to continue to follow up with his healthcare providers to receive appropriate care and treatment for his condition.

Summary:
The patient was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of intellectual deficiency, proximal myopathy, and alterations in liver tests. The patient was diagnosed with suspicion of Danon disease due to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with anomalous pathway. The patient received standard care during the hospital stay with a multidisciplinary team of healthcare providers closely monitoring progress. The patient is being discharged from the hospital with instructions to follow up with his primary physician and/or cardiologist.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
Danon disease is a lysosomal glycogen storage disease caused by a LAMP2 mutation (the c.741+1G>A variant is in LAMP2). In ICD-10-AM it is coded to E74.0, glycogen storage disease. It is an X-linked disorder with cardiomyopathy, myopathy and intellectual disability.

The summary mentions hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, which could point to I42 (cardiomyopathy). However, the diagnosis is Danon disease, and the cardiomyopathy in glycogen storage disease would be coded as I43* as a manifestation, with E74.0 as the underlying cause. The etiology code therefore takes priority as the principal diagnosis.

**E74**
